work_items.title: Native Rust workspace and reproducible builds
work_items.how: Pinned Rust 1.100.0 and locked Cargo graphs. The native runtime uses only the standard library, and its library/binary forbid unsafe code. Development and fuzz dependencies are separate from runtime code.
work_items.verification: Linux debug/release builds and Clippy passed locally and in PR #7.
work_items.limitations: This qualifies the lab toolchain only; crypto, storage and other runtime libraries remain undecided.

work_items.title: Bounded BER / LDAP decoder
work_items.how: Implemented checked definite BER lengths and integer/tag validation without recursion. Frames are capped at 16 KiB, with attribute count/name and DN bounds applied before accepting requests.
work_items.verification: Negative tests cover truncation, malformed lengths/IDs/tags, unsupported controls and attribute limits; generated inputs exercise bounded behavior.
work_items.limitations: Only the declared LDAP subset is decoded; this is not full LDAP or AD conformance.

work_items.title: Read-only RootDSE queries
work_items.how: Implemented empty-DN base searches for objectClass presence. Explicit attribute projection, *, +, 1.1 and typesOnly select static public metadata. No AD capability OIDs or naming contexts are advertised.
work_items.verification: The independent ldap3 client reads supportedLDAPVersion and vendor metadata from the running binary.
work_items.limitations: There are no users, groups, schema, directory state or general searches.

work_items.title: Credential rejection and safe diagnostics
work_items.how: Only anonymous access to public lab metadata succeeds. Credential/SASL binds fail. Parsed request/debug state retains no bind DN or password, and service diagnostics use static messages.
work_items.verification: Tests verify credential rejection, no credential echo in debug/response/stdout/stderr, and unsupported search failures.
work_items.limitations: This is a safeguard, not authentication or password management. There is no TLS; never send real credentials.

work_items.title: TCP framing and session budgets
work_items.how: Implemented fragmented/coalesced frame reads and a loopback-only, single-active-connection listener. Every read/write uses the remaining five-second total deadline; sessions stop after 32 requests.
work_items.verification: Socket tests cover idle deadlines, framing, public-interface refusal and request limits. A malformed peer does not kill the process.
work_items.limitations: The sequential listener is a lab design, not a production availability or throughput claim.

work_items.title: Independent client and packaged-binary checks
work_items.how: A separate Python ldap3 client launches the Rust process on an ephemeral loopback port. CI tests the release binary, then extracts the internal archive and tests that executable again.
work_items.verification: Positive RootDSE, credential denial, scope denial, malformed-peer recovery and extracted-binary checks passed.
work_items.limitations: This is Linux client evidence, not Windows domain join or a deployment qualification.

work_items.title: Property tests and core coverage gate
work_items.how: Added native negative/integration/property tests and instrumented coverage. The actual process is exercised in addition to direct parser tests; the core gate requires at least 90% lines.
work_items.verification: 21 Rust integration/property tests passed. Local measured core line coverage exceeded 90%; Python tooling had 34 passing tests and 98% combined coverage.
work_items.limitations: Core line coverage excludes test/CLI dispatch files. Percentages do not measure coverage of future AD functionality.

work_items.title: Sanitizer fuzz smoke
work_items.how: Added a separate locked libFuzzer target for decode/respond and frame reading, seeded only with synthetic wire data. The PR budget caps iterations, time, input size and RSS.
work_items.verification: 20,000 local address-sanitizer fuzz runs completed without a crash and without changing the lockfiles. Hosted PR #7 fuzz also passed.
work_items.limitations: A bounded fuzz run is not proof that no vulnerability exists. Longer schedules apply after the workflow reaches main.

work_items.title: Native dependency, license and SBOM checks
work_items.how: Cargo deny checks advisories, licenses, sources and dependency bans for core and fuzz graphs, including development/build dependencies. Checksum-pinned Syft catalogs Cargo.lock into a CycloneDX inventory.
work_items.verification: Both dependency audits passed; the generated source inventory was checked for proptest and libfuzzer-sys.
work_items.limitations: The SBOM includes test/fuzz dependencies; it is not a runtime-only or complete OS/stdlib inventory. The project license is still undecided.

work_items.title: Required native and repository CI gates
work_items.how: Added native build/coverage, supply-chain and sanitizer-fuzz jobs behind a reusable fail-closed aggregate. New source scopes must be explicitly registered with checks. Actions/tools/dependencies are pinned or hash-locked.
work_items.verification: All 11 checks in the main-branch CI run passed at merge commit 3a69a6b, following PR #7.
work_items.limitations: Checks run, but GitHub merge protection is not enforced on the current private-repository plan. Passing CI does not establish AD compatibility or production readiness.

work_items.title: Complete phase specifications and traceability
work_items.how: Created 18 phase designs with 180 phase requirements referencing all 130 global capability IDs. CI checks missing phases, unknown/duplicate IDs, empty acceptance and unassigned capabilities.
work_items.verification: The baseline validator and its negative regression cases pass.
work_items.limitations: A consistent document is not passing product evidence; no phase has been accepted.

work_items.title: Threat model and open decision register
work_items.how: Documented component authority, identity/state/replication invariants, attack paths and capacity assumptions. Unresolved choices have owner roles and explicit blocking points.
work_items.verification: Reviewed for internal consistency and linked into phase designs.
work_items.limitations: Named accountable owners, independent assessment, Windows lab, final storage/key choices and measured capacity remain outstanding.

work_items.title: Tested source and lab archive packaging
work_items.how: Source packaging archives the tested commit with deterministic compression and checksum verification. The lab archive is checked after extraction; source release remains license-gated and creates drafts only.
work_items.verification: Committed-source exclusion, unsafe-tag/Git-failure tests and internal archive smoke checks passed.

work_items.title: Bounded LDAP RootDSE filter discovery
work_items.how: Evaluates presence, objectClass descriptor/OID equality and AND/OR/NOT against the fixed public RootDSE. Uses True/False/Undefined semantics, visits every branch, enforces depth 8 / 64 nodes / 256 assertion bytes and never retains assertion bytes.
work_items.verification: Local validation: 28 Rust tests, generated boolean/identifier properties, independent ldap3 positive/empty/unsupported checks, 94.49% core line coverage (filter module 100%) and 20,000 sanitizer-fuzz iterations without a crash.
work_items.limitations: Lab-only synthetic/public data. Other matching rules, general directory/schema queries, DNS, credentials, TLS and Windows domain interoperability remain unimplemented.

work_items.title: Open-PR-aware private progress reporting
work_items.how: Reads open PR descriptions/files/CI state and bounded progress JSON as data. Shows new/changed work and problem records separately from main totals, links PR-head evidence to affected substeps and preserves per-record historical revisions.
work_items.verification: Local validation: 74 Python tests with 98% combined tooling coverage. GitHub Markdown rendering verified that a hostile PR description remained inert and preserved all phase disclosures.
work_items.limitations: Automatic PR refresh activates after merge. Fork structured facts are omitted; metadata has explicit listing limits. Private overlays never enter public HTML artifacts.

work_items.title: Remove unpatched vulnerable tooling dependency path
work_items.how: Removed TypeScript-ESLint and its picomatch path. Retained supported ESLint 10 / TypeScript 6, strict compiler checks and explicit-any AST checks; runs DOM/eval rules on compiler-erased JavaScript without bundling, minification or execution.
work_items.verification: Locked clean install; npm audit reports zero vulnerabilities. Six build/lint tests include typed HTML sinks, eval, explicit-any declarations/casts and safe text rendering; strict typecheck and lint pass.
work_items.limitations: This replaces recommended TypeScript style rules with documented compiler/security policies; it does not claim rule-for-rule style equivalence. PR #16 is merged; main run 44153995669 passed all 12 jobs.

work_items.title: Scope-based phase sizes and explicit owner acceptance reviews
work_items.how: Removed the enforced ten-item sequential quota, retaining unique phase-owned IDs, nonempty requirements/evidence and feature traceability. Renamed broad dashboard substeps to requirements. Documented concrete owner review questions and separate requirement/phase acceptance. Existing scope and stable IDs are preserved. The project owner explicitly approved P01-01 and P01-10 for their stated current-component scopes; reviewer/date/evidence records are stored on both requirements.
work_items.verification: 78 Python tests pass with 98% tooling coverage. Strict types, lint, documentation checks, six build/security-lint tests and 24 desktop/mobile browser tests pass. Synthetic 3/13-item phases exercise rendering, counts and expand-all; model/design fixtures allow unequal counts and noncontiguous IDs. Hosted run 44156039039 did not start: GitHub reported failed recent payments or an insufficient spending limit; this is not a hosted test result.
work_items.limitations: Two scoped requirements (P01-01 and P01-10) are accepted by explicit owner answers on 2026-11-17. These approval records are proposed in PR #18 until merge; the main baseline count updates after merge. The current baseline retains 180 requirements, and full AD functionality and Phase 1 acceptance remain outstanding. Future components must satisfy their own safeguards.

work_items.title: Support public repository dashboard publication and prepare visibility transition
work_items.how: Publisher and PR collector accept either explicit Babel visibility and reject other repository identities or unknown visibility. Retained default-branch-only publication, current-main revision checks, bounded data-only PR imports, metadata-only fork reporting and fast-forward README-only updates. Renamed the publishing workflow and corrected private-only documentation.
work_items.verification: 80 Python tests pass with 98% tooling coverage; strict types, lint, documentation links, actionlint and Zizmor pass. Tests cover public/private publication, unknown visibility, unrelated destinations and public fork metadata isolation. Gitleaks scanned fetched branch history with redacted output and found no leaks.
work_items.limitations: Owner explicitly authorized public visibility, but GitHub rejected the integration’s private=false request with HTTP 403. The repository remains private and hosted CI is still blocked by billing. This PR must merge before default-branch publication supports public visibility. No license was invented and no paid capacity was purchased.

work_items.title: Keep the tested compiler API instead of silently weakening security lint
work_items.how: Reproduced TypeScript 7.0.2 passing typecheck but crashing lint because ScriptTarget.Latest is absent. Restored TypeScript 6.0.3 and its locked tooling graph, retained AST/DOM/eval checks and deferred automatic major compiler proposals until the security-policy API is explicitly migrated. PR #17 now carries this correction instead of an unsupported upgrade.
work_items.verification: Strict compiler checks, ESLint, six build/security-lint fixtures, 24 desktop/mobile browser tests and npm audit all pass locally; audit reports zero vulnerabilities. Hosted full CI is rerun for the corrected PR head.
work_items.limitations: TypeScript 7 is deliberately not adopted. Migration to its different unstable APIs needs a separate qualified change; a passing compiler CLI alone does not establish equivalent security lint.

work_items.title: Verify Pages archives and minimize privileged deployment operations
work_items.how: Read-only preflight validates exact main CI, immutable artifact ID, size and SHA-256 digest. A bounded verifier rejects extra/traversing/symlink files and weak browser policy, then packages only HTML/.nojekyll. The separate Pages/OIDC job has no checkout or project-code execution, attempts Actions-only/HTTPS configuration and rechecks main before deployment. Added no-referrer policy, blocked images, CODEOWNERS, a main ruleset template and verified owner settings. Registered only the named ruleset JSON with object/syntax validation in the CI scope guard; unrelated JSON manifests remain rejected. Shortened the focus summary and compacted phase cards after hosted viewport checks caught overflow.
work_items.verification: 87 Python tests pass with 98% tooling coverage. Negative archive/CSP tests, actual standalone archive verification, strict types/lint, actionlint, Zizmor, six build/lint fixtures and 24 browser tests pass locally. Live current site returned HTTP 200; Pages API confirms HTTPS and environment main-only deployment policy.
work_items.limitations: These stronger deployment changes await PR merge and a successful main workflow run. The integration cannot mutate admin settings (HTTP 403). The job-token Pages configuration step must succeed and read back correctly; no success is claimed in advance. Required review, private vulnerability reporting and other owner settings remain explicit actions. GitHub Pages does not support arbitrary security response headers.

Live API confirms workflow publishing/HTTPS; corrected read-only predicate returns true locally. Workflow lint and Zizmor pass; actual new deployment still requires merge.

work_items.how: Copied the full Apache-2.0 and DCO 1.1 texts from their official publishers; added project notices, incoming contribution policy and consistent Cargo/npm SPDX metadata. Disabled the unpublished-package license-audit exemption. No contributor signature is fabricated.

TypeScript lint/build/security fixtures and npm audit pass with zero vulnerabilities. The owner’s explicit choice is recorded in D-01.

work_items.title: Prepare an isolated Windows reference lab definition without provisioning
work_items.how: Defined two isolated .test networks and six scoped reference/Babel/client/probe machines with bounded resources, no bridge/routes/external DNS/downloads, fresh credentials and blank image metadata. Added a stdlib-only validator and same-PR configuration CI, with denied-safety/topology/resource/image tests and a provisioning/teardown/evidence contract.
work_items.verification: 93 Python tests pass with 98% tooling coverage; the lab validator has 100% measured line/branch coverage. The committed definition validates; require-images rejects the missing image placeholders. No KVM device or qualified Windows host exists in this worker.
work_items.limitations: This is configuration preparation only. No images downloaded, terms accepted, VMs created, infrastructure purchased or Windows operations tested. I04 remains open; exact client builds and two clean real lab runs are required.

work_items.title: Record PostgreSQL selection and a reviewable native state contract
work_items.how: Recorded the owner’s explicit PostgreSQL choice. ADR 0003 assigns identity/schema/ACL/replication semantics to Babel, independent local stores per DC, a proposed atomic journal/audit/idempotency transaction and ordered writer allocation. It explains why ordinary SQL sequence allocation can lose changes below a replicated watermark and specifies kill/retry/recovery qualification.
work_items.verification: Design is linked to D-04/D-05/D-06 and existing Phase 1/3 requirements. Documentation links and phase/model validation pass. Backend-family selection is approved; schema/driver/runtime and durability claims are not marked tested.
work_items.limitations: No database is installed or implemented by this ADR. Key custody, crash/index/locking evidence, AD conflict/RID/FSMO and GPO/SYSVOL contracts remain separate gates. A future backend migration still needs data/recovery/conformance qualification.

work_items.title: Run real PostgreSQL synthetic transaction and process-crash experiments
work_items.how: Added a digest-pinned official PostgreSQL 18 dependency, a bounded synthetic SQL schema and a stdlib Docker/psql controller. State, local journal, audit intent and idempotency commit together under a transactional writer allocator; synthetic UUID/SID identity is immutable. Tests use actual concurrent sessions and SIGKILL/restart. Containers have no network, ports, host binds or privileged mode, with read-only rootfs and scoped cleanup. Added a required runtime CI/coverage job, strict types/lint/security checks and test-image inventory.
work_items.verification: 21 component tests pass against PostgreSQL/psql 18.7; controller branch-inclusive coverage is 93%. Real cases cover collisions/injection/denial, rollback, ordered concurrent commit/rollback, kill before commit, committed-result recovery and idempotent retry after a discarded reply. Actual container isolation and cleanup are asserted. A CycloneDX test-image inventory was generated locally; 97 repository tests pass with 98% coverage.
work_items.limitations: Local and unpublished; the prepared hosted job has not run. This is an isolated SQL experiment, not native directory storage, authentication/Windows ACL, real SID allocation, backup/upgrade, physical power-loss proof, credential protection, AD replication or capacity acceptance. The future Rust driver and production packaging remain unselected/unqualified.

work_items.title: Verify owner-applied repository protections and security settings
work_items.how: Read the active main ruleset and effective branch rules, Pages mode/environment and private-reporting status. Recorded the owner’s explicit confirmation of the three Actions defaults separately from API-verifiable controls. No repository setting or remote branch was changed.
work_items.verification: Ruleset 27498979 is active for refs/heads/main with no bypass, required review/CI and force-push/deletion protection. Private reporting is enabled. Pages is workflow/HTTPS/main-only with admin bypass false. Actions settings remain HTTP 403 and are therefore owner-confirmed, not API-verified.
work_items.limitations: A private report was not submitted and no production phase or independent source-release approval is accepted. The existing source-release environment is missing and separately blocked by I22. Dashboard changes remain local while publication is paused.

work_items.title: Fail source prereleases before an unprotected review environment can be auto-created
work_items.how: Prepared a read-only source-release environment preflight before the environment-bound contents/OIDC job. It requires explicit eligible reviewers, self-review prevention, disabled admin bypass and only v* tag deployments. Missing/inaccessible or weak settings fail instead of allowing normal automatic environment creation.
work_items.verification: Four policy regression tests cover missing/weak review, bypass, tag scope and denied access; helper coverage is 100% within the 97-test repository suite. Actual current GitHub metadata returns no source-release environment and the local checker exits nonzero with an owner action message. Workflow syntax/security checks pass.
work_items.limitations: The source-release environment is still absent. The workflow change is local, not published or executed as hosted release code. It assumes the reviewed release workflow and does not replace owner-controlled release-tag creation or platform protection.

problems.title: Main CI rejected newly vulnerable picomatch tooling graph
problems.detail: Main run 44142657828 failed npm audit for GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf. The advisory affects picomatch through 4.0.7 and no patched version was published when checked.
problems.resolution: PR #16 removed the vulnerable dependency path while retaining supported compiler/ESLint versions and tested DOM/eval/explicit-any checks. Merged main run 44153995669 passed all 12 jobs, including dependency audit.
problems.next_action: Keep all-severity audit enforcement and regression coverage on future tooling updates.
problems.provenance: Recorded development-session evidence and repository/CI observations; no separate public issue was created.

problems.title: Fixed requirement quotas and ambiguous substep acceptance labels
problems.detail: The design validator forced exactly ten sequential requirements per phase, while the report called those broad contracts substeps. Zero recorded acceptances made implemented increments hard to distinguish from owner-reviewed scope.
problems.resolution: Removed the fixed quota, clarified requirement/increment labels and documented scoped owner acceptance questions. The owner answered “Accept this scope” for P01-01 and P01-10; both carry reviewer/date/evidence records. Unequal-size regression tests pass. Phase acceptance remains outstanding.
problems.next_action: Merge the reviewed acceptance records after required checks can run; continue decomposing future work according to scope and dependencies while preserving requirement coverage.
problems.provenance: Project owner requested acceptance questions and said substep counts need not be linear; no separate GitHub issue was created.

problems.title: GitHub Actions jobs blocked before startup by account billing
problems.detail: All jobs in PR #18 CI run 44156039039 have zero executed steps. GitHub annotation: The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased. Automatic dashboard refresh jobs are affected too.
problems.resolution: After the owner made Babel public, main CI run 44175150495 executed all 12 jobs successfully. The earlier account-capacity block no longer prevents this verified public run.
problems.next_action: Monitor actual CI results; public standard runners do not authorize paid capacity or make all platform limits disappear.
problems.provenance: Observed GitHub run 44156039039, check run 134296912744 annotation; no pipeline commands ran.

problems.title: GitHub integration cannot apply the authorized public visibility setting
problems.detail: The project owner explicitly requested public visibility. PATCH /repos/Ise-Tom/Babel with private=false returned HTTP 403, Resource not accessible by integration, despite repository metadata showing admin=true. The repository remained private on readback.
problems.resolution: The owner applied public visibility and merged PR #18. GitHub now reports private=false and visibility=public, and the public-compatible dashboard publisher succeeds. The integration itself still lacks administration permissions.
problems.next_action: Keep visibility changes explicit owner decisions and track remaining settings permissions separately under I18.
problems.provenance: Direct GitHub API response in the authorized visibility-change task on 2026-11-17; no automatic approval-review rejection occurred and no visibility setting was applied.

problems.title: TypeScript 7 removed the compiler API used by security lint
problems.detail: PR #17 run 44154241268 passed typecheck but failed dashboard lint with TypeError reading ScriptTarget.Latest. Local reproduction confirmed the major version no longer exposes the JavaScript compiler API; alternate APIs are unstable and require migration.
problems.resolution: The corrected PR retains TypeScript 6.0.3 and the existing AST/DOM/eval protections, with compatible updates still enabled and automatic compiler majors deferred. Local build, lint, browser and audit checks pass.
problems.next_action: Verify corrected PR CI. Migrate the policy explicitly before upgrading the compiler major; retain malformed-input and security regressions.
problems.provenance: Observed failed hosted job 134361914270 and local reproduction of the same failure; no check was skipped.

problems.title: Repository and Pages controls applied; Actions defaults owner-confirmed
problems.detail: The integration still has restricted administration access. The owner applied the repository security controls: main protection, private vulnerability reporting and Pages main-only deployment with admin bypass disabled are verified through APIs.
problems.resolution: The owner explicitly confirmed read-only Actions defaults, disabled Actions approving PRs and approval for all outside collaborators. These are owner-confirmed because the Actions settings API still returns HTTP 403. No private vulnerability report was submitted or falsely marked exercised. The separate missing source-release environment is tracked under I22.
problems.next_action: Keep the limited integration permissions and periodically reverify actual state. Configure the protected source-release environment under I22 before source prerelease jobs can run.
problems.provenance: Direct GitHub settings API responses and successful public site/deployment observations on 2026-11-17; these are GitHub permission errors, not automatic approval-review rejections.

problems.title: Hosted hardening run caught unregistered ruleset data and viewport overflow
problems.detail: Run 44177850164 rejected the new docs/github-main-ruleset.json under the default-deny component scope policy. The desktop browser check also measured the last phase row at 1015px in a 1000px viewport after the progress summary grew. Local browser validation had preceded that progress-data update.
problems.resolution: Registered that exact non-executable JSON file with readable-object validation and negative tests; other JSON manifests remain rejected. Shortened the focus summary and reduced phase-card spacing. Rebuilt using the final progress data before rerunning browser checks; no CI assertion or source guard was removed.
problems.next_action: Require the corrected full hosted run to pass and keep rebuilding dashboard data before visual checks when progress facts change.

problems.title: Pages deployment attempted an unnecessary denied administration write
problems.detail: After PR #17 merged, main CI passed all 12 jobs and artifact verification passed, but Pages run 44179766192 failed on unconditional PUT /pages. Live settings were already Actions-only with HTTPS; the job token could not administer them.
problems.resolution: The follow-up removes the PUT and retains a fail-closed GET/readback check. Correct existing settings no longer require administration access; insecure settings or failed reads still stop deployment.
problems.next_action: Review/merge the patch and verify the next main Pages deployment; keep owner-only repository security controls explicit under I02/I18.
problems.provenance: Observed complete hosted failure logs and current API state on 2026-11-17; this is a GitHub permission rejection, not automatic approval review.

problems.title: PostgreSQL temporary initialization server looked ready before final startup
problems.detail: The first real container experiment saw pg_isready succeed against the official image’s temporary initialization server before the final database process was available, so the first query failed.
problems.resolution: Readiness now requires the container’s final postgres PID 1 before the socket probe; startup is bounded and failed initialization removes only the owned container/volumes. The final process/crash suite passes.
problems.next_action: Keep the startup barrier while using this pinned image and requalify it on reviewed image changes.
problems.provenance: Observed local real-container failure and subsequent successful 21-test integration run; not a Windows or production failure claim.

problems.title: Protected source-release review environment is missing
problems.detail: GET environments/source-release returned HTTP 404. Main protection, Pages restrictions and private reporting are applied, but they do not provide the independent release-environment approval required for source prereleases.
problems.next_action: Owner creates source-release with eligible independent reviewers, prevent self-review, no admin bypass and custom v* tag-only deployment policy, and controls release-tag creation. Then run the read-only checker. The prepared workflow must be reviewed/published before it enforces this preflight on GitHub.
problems.provenance: Direct current GitHub metadata and an expected nonzero local preflight result; no environment, tag or release was created.

focus_summary: Synthetic PostgreSQL transaction and crash tests pass. Native directory storage, key custody, AD replication and the Windows lab remain unqualified.
